title: Latency SLI drift detector + load harness: per-route/model/region percentiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Deliver a robust pipeline and dashboards to compute p95 and p99 latency SLIs partitioned by API route, served model variant, and region, and wire these into our load-testing/regression harness so weekly jobs detect SLI drift automatically. This ticket covers metrics design, ingestion changes, dashboard surfaces, and automation for regression detection alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregated p95 and p99 percentiles are available in the metrics store keyed by {route, model, region} for 1m, 5m, 1h windows
Grafana dashboard shows heatmaps and time-series for tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 with per-route/model/region filters
Weekly regression job runs load harness with stable prompt set and fails CI if p95 increases beyond configured threshold
Alerting rules created: SLI_drift_{route,model,region} with knobs for baseline and anomaly window
Bench harness can emit synthetic traffic labels so metrics attribute to load-test vs production traffic
tasks: Design histogram/reservoir approach: HDR histograms at ingestion vs percentile_approx in ClickHouse
Add tagging to serving runtime to emit route/model/region labels on latency metrics
Instrument load harness to tag synthetic traffic and capture tokens/sec and latency per request
Implement streaming aggregation job to roll histograms into 1m/5m buckets and write to metrics DB
Create Grafana dashboard + templated variables for route/model/region and tokens/sec overlay
Add CI job that runs weekly load-test, computes delta against baseline, and files regression alert if >10% p95 increase
Run privacy/security review for metric labels (no PII) and K8s secrets access for harness runners
notes: Design trade-offs: storing raw per-request traces for percentiles is high-cardinality; prefer HDR histograms produced at edge (runtime) to keep ingestion volume under control.

We debated server-side percentile_approx vs client-side TDigest. Chosen path: runtime emits HDR histogram buckets and backend uses group_by on pre-aggregated buckets in ClickHouse. This gives accurate p95/p99 at low cost and easy rollups.
Cardinality: model variants + canary labels + region increased labels. Limit models included in default dashboards to top-50 by qps; other models tucked behind 'show low-volume' toggle.
Tokens/sec: tokens produced per second will be tracked as a separate gauge with same partition keys and shown alongside latency series to correlate throughput vs latency shifts.
Retention: keep detailed 1m histograms for 90 days, 1h rollups for 365 days. This is in line with runtime-2.4 storage budget.
Instrumentation links: runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/458, metrics consumer PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics/pull/319
Draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/3xP7K/latency-sli-by-route-model-region (prototype panel IDs in comments)
risks: High cardinality of model+route+region leading to increased metrics costs
Ingestion performance impact if runtime emits high-resolution histograms for every request
False positives from noisy networks or cold-starts causing regression CI churn
Coordinating rollout across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments requires backward-compatible metric formats
mitigation_plan: Emit HDR buckets at a coarse resolution and enable fine buckets behind a runtime flag for canary runs
Add sampler in runtime so only X% of low-QPS routes emit full histograms unless explicitly opted-in
Baseline computation uses median-of-week rather than single-run to reduce false positives
Compatibility layer: runtime will emit a versioned metric label 'latency_metric_v=2' and old consumers continue to work

open_questions: What default threshold should trigger a regression CI failure? current proposal: 10% p95 increase or absolute +200ms, whichever is larger
Should we include median (p50) in regression rules or only tail metrics? PM prefers p95/p99 only for alerting but ops wants p50 for capacity planning
How to display low-sample routes on the dashboard (hide vs show with confidence interval)?
Do private/on-prem deployments need a local Grafana configuration template or will hosted dashboards suffice?
